title: What If 5 Cats Were Let Loose on an Island? 3,400 Cats Later, a War Began

scenes.text: What if five cats were let loose on an island? It took 42 years to undo.
1949: five house cats arrive at a weather station on Marion Island to catch mice.
By 1977, there were about 3,400 feral cats, eating around 450,000 seabirds a year.
First, scientists released a cat virus. Within five years numbers fell to about 600. The survivors were immune.
Then came night hunters with shotguns, traps, and poisoned bait. Over a thousand cats in seven years.
The last cat was trapped in 1991. The petrels came back. The mice never left. They're now eating albatross chicks.

description:
What if five cats were released on an island? In 1949 five house cats were brought to the weather station on sub-Antarctic Marion Island to control mice. By 1977 there were about 3,400 feral cats killing an estimated 450,000 burrowing petrels a year.
The eradication took from 1977 to 1991: a feline panleucopaenia virus cut the population to about 600 by 1982, then night hunting with shotguns, trapping and poisoning finished the job. The last cat was trapped in July 1991, and for 27 years it was the largest island ever cleared of cats. Petrel breeding success rose from near zero to over 60 percent, but the mice remain and now attack seabird chicks.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: The next project is removing the mice, from an island of 290 square kilometres. Which island introduction went most wrong? Drop your own what-if below.
